why: A set to remember what exists: put every value in a set, start counting only at values v whose v-1 is absent (the start of a run), and extend v+1, v+2, ... by lookups. Each value is touched a constant number of times, so O(n) without sorting.
hints: Sorting gives O(n log n). What question about a value could you answer in O(1) with a set?
A run of consecutive values has exactly one start: the value v with v-1 missing. Only start counting from such values.
seen = set(nums); for v in seen: if v-1 not in seen: walk while v+len in seen. Track the best length. Every value is visited by at most one walk, so O(n).
pitfalls: Duplicates count once; iterate over the set, not the original array, to avoid repeated walks.
Without the 'v-1 not in seen' check the algorithm degrades to O(n^2) on a long run.
An empty array (if given) has answer 0.
constraints:
• 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
  • Bounds are not stated in the source; these are the standard LeetCode 128 bounds. Aim for O(n).
